note The sweep's 0 Hz point is answered by circuitRF's conduction solve of the conductors, not by the 3D solver.
note 4 overlapping conductor shape(s) were merged into 2 — copper that overlaps on one level is one conductor, in 3D as in the planar model.
note Resistive film 'Resistor' on 'TFR Level' is a sheet at σ = 4E+05 S/m × t = 50 nm, 50 Ω/sq: for a sheet only the product is physical.
note Dielectric 'MIM Dielectric' exists only where 'Nitride' is drawn, and nothing is drawn there, so it is not in the 3D problem.
note Port 1 ('1') at (0, 0 µm) was taken to be on the conductor's low-x (left) end (inferred from the nearest conductor boundary) of level 1 ('Metal1'), driving current in the +x direction, at 50 Ω.
note Port 2 ('2') at (800, 0 µm) was taken to be on the conductor's high-x (right) end (inferred from the nearest conductor boundary) of level 1 ('Metal1'), driving current in the −x direction, at 50 Ω.
note Port 1 at its line's end is a wave port returning through 'Backside Metal' (the air box's floor), below the line: the nearest ground-reference plane with metal under the port.
note Port 2 at its line's end is a wave port returning through 'Backside Metal' (the air box's floor), below the line: the nearest ground-reference plane with metal under the port.
note Port 1's wave-port region is clipped to the air box's xmin face; the box is smaller than the sizing rule asks for there.
note Port 1 is a wave port on the air box's xmin face: 800 × 706.25 µm (13.7329 line widths × 8 heights, the sizing rule's), its reference plane on the face.
note Port 2's wave-port region is clipped to the air box's xmax face; the box is smaller than the sizing rule asks for there.
note Port 2 is a wave port on the air box's xmax face: 800 × 706.25 µm (13.7329 line widths × 8 heights, the sizing rule's), its reference plane on the face.
note 2 conductor piece(s) are sheets because this setup states Conductors: Sheets, the planar model's own idealisation: each carries its conductivity and thickness rather than a meshed volume.
note The air box's floor is 'Backside Metal' as a PEC plane at 3 µm: it is the lowest ground-reference conductor, nothing is drawn on it and nothing is drawn below it. The AirBox ZMin padding does not apply to a floor on the plane.
